title: Constant-group sheaf torsors and the quotient atlas fibre
statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with the displayed sheafification and slice sheafifications available, $H$ a group, and $A$ an $H$-action in sheaves of sets. The regular sheaf is the constant sheaf $\underline H$, with the sheafification of its left translation action. A sheaf action $P$ is locally regular if over each $U$ there is a $J$-covering sieve such that on the slice over every arrow in it $P$ is equivariantly isomorphic to $\underline H$. Define the quotient groupoid as the core of the full subcategory of equivariant arrows $P\to A$ with locally regular source; its arrows are equivariant sheaf isomorphisms commuting with the maps to $A$. At a terminal test object $t$ a section $z$ defines the orbit map $h\mapsto h\cdot z$ by the constant-sheaf adjunction; the action law makes this map equivariant. This specifies the trivial-torsor atlas $q(z)$. Its fibre over $\xi=(P,v)$ is the iso-comma 2-fibre product [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] of $q$ with $\xi$, computed in the ambient core of equivariant maps (the full inclusion preserves these isomorphisms). Evaluation is $\eta\mapsto\eta(1)$. Restriction to $C/U$ is precomposition with the slice forgetful functor, including the action and equivariant map. Define the atlas fibre and its evaluation over every such slice. All these are actual constructions; the sole postponed orbit-map equivariance proof is the action-law consequence above.
